newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada ratifies Hague adoption convention.
newsitem.headline: Canada ratifies Hague adoption convention.

text.p: Canada announced on Wednesday it had ratified a convention tightening rules on international adoptions to try to prevent abuse.

The Hague convention on intercountry adoption provides a "mechanism that is open and less costly than the current system (and) does not involve any improper financial or other gains," Justice Minister Allan Rock said in a statement.
A system of cooperation between member states would prevent the abduction, sale or trafficking in children, the statement said.
Would-be adoptive parents would apply to a "central authority" in their countries which would liaise with a similar authority in a country where children are up for adoption.

The original idea was to rule out private organisations as much as possible. But the Canadian statement said private intermediaries could continue to perform certain functions as long as they got authorisation from the countries in which they operated.
It said 20,000 intercountry adoptions take place each year, 2,000 involving Canadians.

Sixty-six states signed the 1993 convention. Apart from Canada, those that have ratified it so far are Burkina Faso, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Romania, Sri Lanka, Spain and Venezuela.
